key_insight: Latent PDE mapping lets physics-informed models learn on a fixed latent geometry while correctly accounting for deformed physical geometries, improving generalization from very few training shapes.
engineering_relevance: This can make surrogate models for PDE-based engineering simulation more data-efficient and more transferable across changing shapes or patient-specific geometries.
method: Pull back PDE residuals and boundary conditions from each physical geometry to a predefined latent domain using the deformation gradient.
Compute geometry-consistent shape gradients automatically within physics-informed neural networks and deep operator networks.
Apply the approach to the anisotropic Aliev-Panfilov cardiac electrophysiology PDE in 2D and 3D.
evidence_signal: The authors trained on only 15 geometries and report about a 4–6× reduction in mean relative L2 error on select geometric families, with modest training overhead and negligible inference cost.
watch_item: Benefits were not uniform across all geometry parameterizations, so performance may depend on the deformation family and how well the latent mapping matches the geometry variation.
paper_title: Latent PDE mapping for efficient physics-informed learning across geometries with limited data
